curriculum.rationale: Seven measured sources found the representation before any lower-integrity source exists: eegmmidb (64ch, 109 participants), sleep-edfx (2 bipolar derivations, 78 participants, enabled for the first time), ds000117 (70ch cap, 2 participants), ds004024 resting (64ch, 2 participants), ds002336 (parcel BOLD, 10 participants), and the two new attachment kinds -- ds000117_behaviour (boundary_output) and ds004024_perturb (a measured intervention). `behaviour.*` and `eeg_montages.*` are granted at tier 1 because tier-1 sources are the only ones with evidence about them.

Sized by what is being estimated, not by corpus size: per-channel gain, offset and noise floor across four montages. A calibration source has tiny measurement variance and would win a pure inverse-variance contest, which is why it is admitted late and narrowly. Note the tier-2 grants now name the montage heads too -- without that, three of the four montages' nuisance would be calibrated by nobody.
The 9-family partition and the connectome scale enter here, after the measured sources have already fixed the representation they modulate.

The amortised posterior is founded here and only here. No measured recording carries a theta label, so no tier-1 source can found it -- not as a wiring gap but in principle. That is the founding exemption `configs/curriculum/tiers.yaml` already grants to `posterior.*`, and this is the stage that uses it. Tier 4 does NOT reach `eeg.*`, `eeg_montages.*`, `bold.*` or `behaviour.*`: a simulator may not calibrate an instrument.

The 1 -> 4 -> 1 return. The simulator is withdrawn and the measured sources have the last word, so the final weights are conditioned on evidence rather than on the generator. `tms_drive.*` is granted here and nowhere else: the pulse's amplitude and its profile over motor parcels are learned against the measured evoked response, and letting a simulator stage touch them would fit the drive to synthetic dynamics.

arm.justification: Heterogeneous region-indexed state with per-family operators (`family_state: true`). Run 2 was nominally this arm and could not be read as one, because the family-indexed modules never received a gradient.

config.notes: SC-WBD-003. Seven measured sources, four observation montages, and the first boundary_output and measured perturbation in the mixture. Trained on this box: 1.1 TB free, all data in place, 121 GB unified. The second GB10 (spark-ec4d) was probed and rejected -- 184 GB free of 3.7 TB against a 177 GB data directory leaves no room for checkpoints, and nothing in scwbd/foundation is distributed anyway.

lead_field.note: ANALYTIC SINGLE-SPHERE LEAD FIELD, NOT A HEAD MODEL. Radial dipoles in a homogeneous conducting sphere with electrodes at real 10-10 montage positions (MNE standard_1005). Supports no source-localisation or individual-anatomy claim.

sensor_to_parcel.note: Assimilation input only. The likelihood is evaluated in sensor space; this projection supports no source-localisation claim.

posterior_calibration.note: Calibration measured against the SAME simulator that generated the training corpus. It certifies self-consistency of the amortized posterior under simulator-conditioned evidence only, and is NOT evidence of biological validity or of correct inference on real data.
posterior_calibration.sampling: backend-stratified, fold-proportional with a floor per backend

backend_comparison.note: The learned operator is the equal-capacity control for every mechanistic claim (Appendix D). Matching a family's trajectories is not evidence that the family is neurally realized.

real_eeg_holdout.sampling: participant-stratified, evenly spaced within participant; budget fixed by participants, not batches

real_split.verification: verified against the fingerprint recorded in the checkpoint

individualization.reason: no individualizer on the trainer (population model)

real_eeg_holdout.metric: gaussian NLL, nats per channel per sample, sensor space, participant-clustered 95% CI
real_eeg_holdout.estimator: plug-in at posterior mean (matches the baselines' plug-in form)

describe.name: persistence
assumptions: the signal is locally constant on the prediction horizon
residual variance is stationary across participants and sessions
describe.falsifies_comparison_if: If the foundation model does not beat persistence by a margin whose participant-clustered interval excludes zero, the predictive claim is explained by autocorrelation alone and must be withdrawn.

describe.name: ar16
assumptions: per-channel linear, stationary, Gaussian-innovation dynamics
one set of coefficients for the whole population (no subject fitting)
channels are conditionally independent given their own past
context is at least 16 samples long
describe.falsifies_comparison_if: If a per-channel AR fitted on the same training windows matches the foundation model's held-out NLL, then the claimed benefit of connectome structure and per-region state reduces to per-channel spectral continuation and the structural claim is unsupported.

describe.name: var4
assumptions: linear, stationary, dense lagged coupling between all channels
one coupling matrix for the whole population (no subject fitting)
ridge/rank regularisation is the right capacity control at this n
sensor-space coupling stands in for source-space coupling
describe.falsifies_comparison_if: If a dense VAR fitted on the same windows matches the foundation model, then cross-channel structure did not have to be anatomical: an unconstrained linear coupling suffices, and the connectome-structured claim loses its evidential basis.

describe.name: population_gaussian
assumptions: one stationary Gaussian describes the whole population
temporal structure is exhausted by a per-channel lag-1 autocovariance
no participant identity, session, montage or anatomy is used
describe.falsifies_comparison_if: If the foundation model does not beat the population Gaussian on a participant's held-out future, then including that participant's data was not personalization, and no individualization claim may be made.

describe.name: subject_specific_ar
assumptions: each participant has enough training windows to fit their own model
the participant's training and held-out windows are exchangeable (same session-level nonstationarity would flatter this baseline)
participant identity is known at test time
describe.falsifies_comparison_if: If a model fitted on a participant alone predicts that participant's held-out future as well as the population-pretrained foundation model, then cross-participant pretraining transferred nothing on this port and the foundation claim fails regardless of the aggregate score.
describe.note: n_parameters is the SUM over participants: this baseline is not capacity-matched to a single shared model and must not be presented as if it were. It is reported so the asymmetry is visible.

describe.name: dense_gru_matched
assumptions: the optimiser found a solution worth comparing against (check loss_history before quoting this baseline)
parameter count is a fair capacity proxy at matched training steps and matched data
no connectome, adjacency or per-region state is used -- by construction
its variance head is fitted in-sample, which flatters it relative to the held-out-calibrated linear baselines
describe.falsifies_comparison_if: If an unstructured network with the same parameter count, data and training budget matches the foundation model's held-out NLL, then the connectome and per-region state are decorative and the structural claim must be withdrawn.
describe.variance_calibration: heteroscedastic head trained in-sample on free-running rollouts (rollout_len=22)

describe.name: scwbd-003
describe.variance_calibration: state-dependent: sourced from X^uncertainty via the observation interface, plus a separately parameterised per-channel instrument floor

noise_floor.role: per-channel instrument floor (electrode impedance, amplifier noise)

real_eeg_holdout.mse_interpretation: Paired participant-clustered 95% interval of the per-window MSE difference (scwbd minus baseline; negative favours SC-WBD). This is the CONDITIONAL MEAN, scored separately from the NLL on purpose: the two can and do disagree. Run 1 reported only the NLL and therefore filed a model with the lowest MSE of all seven arms as beaten by five of six. The difference between the two verdicts is the predictive variance, and it is a defect in the variance channel rather than in the forecast.
real_eeg_holdout.verdict: No baseline beats scwbd-003 on the paired participant-clustered 95% interval of the per-window NLL difference
real_eeg_holdout.interpretation: The verdict is the PAIRED interval, not the ranking: two overlapping marginal intervals can still admit a decisive paired difference, and a lower point estimate is not a claim. Models listed in `inconclusive_vs_scwbd` are neither better nor worse at this sample size. Window-level generalisation is not individual generalisation.
